title: Payment Gateway V2 Architecture - MFS Internal Wiki
text:
Payment Gateway V2 Architecture

The MFS Payment Gateway V2 is a modernized payment processing platform deployed on OpenShift in the mfs-prod namespace. It handles payment tokenization, multi-currency processing, and settlement operations for Meridian Financial Services.

System Overview
The gateway processes card-present and card-not-present transactions through a microservices architecture. Key services include the tokenization service, retry handler with circuit breaker, currency exchange service, and settlement batch processor.

Component Topology
The production deployment consists of:
- mfs-pay-pod-01: Primary payment processing (active)
- mfs-pay-pod-02: Secondary payment processing (active)
- mfs-pay-pod-03: Overflow payment processing (standby)
- mfs-vault-pod-01: Token vault and HSM integration
- mfs-settle-pod-01: Settlement batch processing

All pods run in the mfs-prod OpenShift namespace with a staging mirror in mfs-staging.

Service Accounts
The gateway uses dedicated service accounts for authentication and authorization:
- svc-payment-api: Payment gateway API operations, authenticated via OAuth2 client credentials
- svc-token-vault: HSM key retrieval and token vault operations, authenticated via mTLS + OAuth2
- svc-settlement: Settlement batch processing and file generation
- svc-notification-svc: Alert and notification delivery for payment events and reconciliation discrepancies

Database Architecture
Primary database: mfs_payments_db (PostgreSQL 15) hosted on pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal. Contains tables for card_tokens, cardholder_data (encrypted with AES-256-GCM), retry_ledger, currency_rates, settlement_batches, settlement_records, and gateway_ledger.

Audit database: mfs_audit_db (PostgreSQL 15) co-located on pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal. Stores token_audit_log, conversion_audit, and reconciliation_results.

Deployment Model
Deployments are managed through OpenShift with rolling updates. Change management follows the ServiceNow ITSM process (standard and normal changes). Recent deployments include CHG0090101 (tokenization), CHG0090102 (retry handler), CHG0090201 (encryption at rest), and CHG0090301 (settlement batch).

title: Runbook: Payment Gateway Timeouts - MFS Internal Wiki
text:
Runbook: Payment Gateway Timeouts

This runbook covers the diagnosis and resolution of payment processing timeout incidents on the MFS Payment Gateway.

Symptom Detection
Timeout incidents are typically detected via:
- Grafana alert: Payment API Latency P99 > 200ms (alert-pay-latency)
- Datadog monitor: Payment API Latency P99 (monitor 550001)
- Kibana dashboard: Payment Gateway Performance (dashboard-pay-gateway-perf)
- Customer reports of payment failures or slow checkout

Triage Steps
1. Check current P99 latency on Grafana Payment Gateway SLOs dashboard
2. Identify affected pods: oc get pods -n mfs-prod -l app=mfs-payment-gateway
3. Check pod resource utilization (CPU, memory, network)
4. Review recent deployments in ServiceNow change records
5. Check database connection status to pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal

Common Root Causes

1. Connection Pool Exhaustion (most common)
After the tokenization deployment (CHG0090101), connection pool exhaustion was observed on mfs-pay-pod-01 due to longer-running tokenization queries against mfs_payments_db. The INC0080101 incident was resolved by increasing the HikariCP connection pool from 20 to 50 connections and adding a 3-second query timeout.

Diagnosis: Check HikariCP metrics via Prometheus - hikari_connections_active should be below maximum-pool-size.

2. HSM Session Saturation
Token vault latency degradation (INC0080102) was traced to insufficient PKCS#11 session pool size on mfs-vault-pod-01 after the encryption-at-rest deployment (CHG0090201). The svc-token-vault service account sessions were saturated at 5 concurrent sessions.

Diagnosis: Check HSM session metrics on mfs-vault-pod-01. Session pool should be set to 20.

3. Circuit Breaker Tripped
If the retry handler circuit breaker is in OPEN state, new payment requests are immediately rejected. Check circuit breaker state via GET /actuator/circuitbreakers on the affected pod.

Resolution: Circuit breaker auto-recovers via half-open probe every 30 seconds. If underlying issue persists, address root cause first.

Resolution Procedures
- Connection pool: Update ConfigMap spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size and restart deployment
- HSM sessions: Update svc-token-vault PKCS#11 session pool configuration
- Circuit breaker: Resolve underlying failure, breaker recovers automatically

Escalation Path
- L1: DevOps & SRE - Li Wei (lwei), Raj Patel (rpatel)
- L2: Platform Engineering - Sarah Chen (schen), David Okoye (dokoye)
- L3: Payment Services - Marcus Rivera (mrivera), Alex Kim (akim)

Post-Incident Review
All P2+ incidents require a post-incident review within 48 hours. Document timeline, root cause, resolution, and preventive measures in Confluence.

title: Payment Gateway API v2 - Swagger UI - MFS API Portal
text:
Payment Gateway API v2

OpenAPI 3.0 specification for the MFS Payment Gateway API v2.

Base URL: https://api.mfs.internal/payment/v2
Authentication: OAuth2 Client Credentials via svc-payment-api service account

Tokenization
POST /api/v2/tokens - Create a payment token from cardholder PAN. Returns an irreversible PCI DSS v4.0 compliant token.
GET /api/v2/tokens/{token_id} - Retrieve token metadata (last four digits, brand, creation date). Never returns raw PAN data.

Payments
POST /api/v2/payments - Process a payment using a previously created token. Supports idempotency keys for safe retries.
POST /api/v2/payments/{payment_id}/retry - Retry a failed payment with circuit breaker protection.
GET /api/v2/payments/{payment_id}/status - Check payment processing status.

Currency
GET /api/v2/currencies/rates - Get current FX exchange rates for supported currencies (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, CHF).
POST /api/v2/payments/convert - Process a payment with automatic currency conversion.

Settlement
POST /api/v2/settlements/batch - Trigger a settlement batch for pending transactions. Requires svc-settlement service account.
GET /api/v2/settlements/{batch_id} - Get settlement batch status.

Authentication
All endpoints require a valid OAuth2 bearer token obtained via client credentials flow using the svc-payment-api service account.

Error Codes
PAY-001: Invalid token
PAY-002: Insufficient funds
PAY-003: Currency not supported
PAY-004: Duplicate idempotency key
PAY-005: Circuit breaker open
PAY-006: Settlement batch in progress

title: mfs_payments_db Schema Documentation - MFS Internal Wiki
text:
mfs_payments_db Schema Documentation

Schema documentation for the MFS Payments database hosted on PostgreSQL 15.

Connection Details
Host: pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal
Port: 5432
Database: mfs_payments_db
Service accounts with access: svc-payment-api (read/write), svc-token-vault (read/write to cardholder_data), svc-settlement (read/write to settlement tables)
Connection pool: HikariCP with max 50 connections per pod (updated after INC0080101)

Tables

card_tokens
Stores tokenized payment card references. Created by TokenizationService.
Columns: token_id (PK, varchar), encrypted_pan (bytea), last_four (varchar(4)), brand (varchar), cardholder_name_hash (varchar), created_at (timestamp), expires_at (timestamp)
Index: idx_card_tokens_created_at on created_at

cardholder_data
Stores encrypted cardholder data (PCI DSS Req 3.4). All sensitive columns encrypted with AES-256-GCM.
Columns: id (PK, bigserial), token_id (FK to card_tokens), encrypted_pan (bytea), encrypted_cvv (bytea), encrypted_expiry (bytea), encryption_key_id (varchar), iv (bytea), auth_tag (bytea), created_at (timestamp)
Encryption: AES-256-GCM via pgcrypto extension, keys managed by HSM through svc-token-vault

retry_ledger
Tracks idempotent retry state for payment operations.
Columns: idempotency_key (PK, varchar), transaction_id (varchar), merchant_id (varchar), attempt_count (int), last_attempt_at (timestamp), status (varchar), circuit_breaker_state (varchar)

currency_rates
Caches FX exchange rates with 60-second TTL.
Columns: id (PK, serial), source_currency (varchar(3)), target_currency (varchar(3)), rate (decimal), fetched_at (timestamp), expires_at (timestamp)

gateway_ledger
Master ledger for all payment transactions processed by the gateway.
Columns: payment_id (PK, varchar), token_id (FK), amount (decimal), currency (varchar(3)), merchant_id (varchar), status (varchar), idempotency_key (varchar), created_at (timestamp), completed_at (timestamp)

settlement_batches
Settlement batch metadata.
Columns: batch_id (PK, varchar), status (varchar), transaction_count (int), total_amount (decimal), currency (varchar(3)), acquirer (varchar), created_at (timestamp), completed_at (timestamp)

settlement_records
Individual settlement records linked to batches.
Columns: id (PK, bigserial), batch_id (FK), payment_id (FK to gateway_ledger), amount (decimal), currency (varchar(3)), merchant_id (varchar), status (varchar), settled_at (timestamp)

Extensions
- pgcrypto: Enabled for column-level encryption (CHG0090201)
- pg_stat_statements: Query performance monitoring

Backup and Recovery
Daily automated backups at 02:00 UTC. Point-in-time recovery available via WAL archiving. RPO: 5 minutes, RTO: 30 minutes.

title: Payment Gateway SLOs - Grafana - MFS Monitoring
text:
Payment Gateway SLOs Dashboard

Real-time SLO monitoring for the MFS Payment Gateway deployed in the mfs-prod OpenShift namespace.

Payment API Latency P99
Current P99 latency across all payment gateway pods (mfs-pay-pod-01, mfs-pay-pod-02, mfs-pay-pod-03). SLO target: < 200ms. Data source: MFS Prometheus (prometheus.mfs.internal:9090).
Query: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(payment_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace='mfs-prod'}[5m]))
Alert: Fires when P99 > 200ms for 5 consecutive minutes (alert-pay-latency). Notifies DevOps & SRE team.

Payment Success Rate
Percentage of successful payment transactions. SLO target: > 99.9%. Includes all payment processing endpoints authenticated via svc-payment-api service account.
Query: sum(rate(payment_api_requests_total{status='success',namespace='mfs-prod'}[5m])) / sum(rate(payment_api_requests_total{namespace='mfs-prod'}[5m])) * 100

Tokenization Throughput
Token creation rate per second across all payment pods. Reflects tokenization workload via TokenizationService backed by svc-token-vault and HSM on mfs-vault-pod-01.

Circuit Breaker Status
Current state of the payment retry circuit breaker on each pod. States: 0=CLOSED (healthy), 1=OPEN (tripped), 2=HALF_OPEN (probing). Circuit breaker opens after 5 consecutive failures, probes every 30 seconds.

title: mfs_payments_db - Table Reference
text:
mfs_payments_db - Table Reference

Complete table reference for mfs_payments_db on pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal.

payments
Core payments table tracking all transaction lifecycle states.
Columns: id (PK, uuid), amount (decimal(19,4)), currency (varchar(3)), status (varchar - pending/authorized/captured/failed/refunded), merchant_id (varchar), created_at (timestamptz), updated_at (timestamptz)
Indexes: idx_payments_merchant_id, idx_payments_status, idx_payments_created_at

payment_methods
Payment method details linked to individual payments.
Columns: id (PK, uuid), payment_id (FK to payments), type (varchar - card/bank/wallet), last_four (varchar(4)), token_id (FK to tokens)
Index: idx_payment_methods_payment_id

tokens
Tokenized cardholder data with HSM key references.
Columns: id (PK, uuid), pan_hash (varchar(64)), token_value (varchar), created_at (timestamptz), hsm_key_id (varchar)
Index: idx_tokens_pan_hash

idempotency_keys
Idempotency key tracking for safe payment retries.
Columns: key (PK, varchar(64)), payment_id (FK to payments), created_at (timestamptz), expires_at (timestamptz)
Index: idx_idempotency_keys_expires_at

webhook_registrations
Merchant webhook registration configurations.
Columns: id (PK, uuid), merchant_id (varchar), url (text), events (jsonb - array of subscribed event types), secret_vault_path (varchar - path in vault.mfs.internal for HMAC signing secret), created_at (timestamptz)
Indexes: idx_webhook_registrations_merchant_id

webhook_delivery_log
Delivery attempt log for all webhook dispatches.
Columns: id (PK, uuid), registration_id (FK to webhook_registrations), event_id (varchar), status (varchar - pending/delivered/failed/dlq), http_status (int), latency_ms (int), created_at (timestamptz)
Indexes: idx_webhook_delivery_log_registration_id, idx_webhook_delivery_log_status

webhook_dlq
Dead letter queue for webhook deliveries that exhausted all retries.
Columns: id (PK, uuid), delivery_log_id (FK to webhook_delivery_log), payload (jsonb), error (text), retry_count (int), created_at (timestamptz)
Index: idx_webhook_dlq_created_at

analytics_aggregates
Pre-computed analytics aggregates for dashboard queries.
Columns: id (PK, uuid), dimension_key (varchar - merchant_id or currency), time_bucket (timestamptz - hourly buckets), transaction_count (int), success_count (int), failure_count (int), avg_settlement_ms (decimal)
Indexes: idx_analytics_aggregates_dimension_key, idx_analytics_aggregates_time_bucket

settlement_batches
Settlement batch metadata for reconciliation.
Columns: id (PK, uuid), batch_date (date), merchant_id (varchar), total_amount (decimal(19,4)), status (varchar - pending/processing/completed/failed), created_at (timestamptz)
Indexes: idx_settlement_batches_merchant_id, idx_settlement_batches_batch_date

Service Accounts:
- svc-payment-api: read/write access to all tables
- svc-analytics: read-only access to payments, analytics_aggregates, settlement_batches

title: mfs-payments Namespace - Pod Overview
text:
mfs-payments Namespace - Pod Overview

Pod topology for mfs-payments namespace on ocp-prod-east.mfs.internal cluster.

Pod Topology

mfs-pay-pod-01
Workloads: payment processing, tokenization, webhook dispatch
Replicas: 4
Resources: 2 CPU / 4Gi memory per replica
Status: Running

mfs-pay-pod-02
Workloads: payment processing secondary
Replicas: 2
Resources: 2 CPU / 4Gi memory per replica
Status: Running

mfs-pay-pod-03
Workloads: analytics workload
Replicas: 2
Resources: 1 CPU / 2Gi memory per replica
Status: Running

Services

mfs-payment-gateway
Type: ClusterIP
Port: 8080
Targets: mfs-pay-pod-01, mfs-pay-pod-02
Selector: app=mfs-payment-gateway

mfs-analytics
Type: ClusterIP
Port: 8081
Targets: mfs-pay-pod-03
Selector: app=mfs-analytics

ConfigMaps and Secrets

ConfigMaps:
- payment-config: Payment processing configuration (timeouts, retry limits, circuit breaker thresholds)
- webhook-config: Webhook dispatch configuration (delivery timeouts, max retries, DLQ settings)
- analytics-config: Analytics aggregation configuration (time buckets, dimension keys, retention)

Secrets:
- payment-db-credentials: PostgreSQL credentials for pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal (rotated via vault.mfs.internal)
- webhook-signing-keys: HMAC signing keys for webhook payload signatures (synced from vault.mfs.internal)

Ingress
api-gateway.mfs.internal -> mfs-payment-gateway service (port 8080)
TLS termination at ingress controller with Let's Encrypt certificate

title: Payment Gateway - Incident Response Playbook
text:
Payment Gateway - Incident Response Playbook

Comprehensive incident response playbook for the MFS Payment Gateway.

P1 Response SLA
- Acknowledge: 15 minutes from alert firing
- Mitigate: 1 hour from acknowledgement
- Resolve: 4 hours from mitigation (best effort)
- Post-incident review: within 48 hours of resolution

Escalation Path
1. On-call engineer: payments-oncall PagerDuty rotation (primary responder)
2. Squad lead: Arjun Deshmukh (payments squad lead, available 08:00-22:00 IST)
3. Platform: Marcus Thompson (platform engineering lead, available 08:00-20:00 EST)
4. VP Engineering: David Kim (final escalation, P1 only)

Diagnostic Tools
- Grafana: payment-gateway-slo dashboard (https://grafana.mfs.internal/d/pay-gateway-slos) - latency P99, success rate, circuit breaker state
- Kibana: query 'service:mfs-payment-gateway AND level:ERROR' for error log analysis (https://kibana.mfs.internal)
- Datadog APM: distributed traces for payment request lifecycle (https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?service=mfs-payment-gateway)
- OpenShift console: pod health and resource utilization on ocp-prod-east.mfs.internal

Common Issues and Resolution

1. Database Connection Exhaustion
Symptom: Increasing latency and connection timeout errors in application logs.
Diagnosis: Check pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal connection count via pg_stat_activity. Compare active connections against max_connections (200) and HikariCP pool size (50 per pod).
Resolution: If connection usage exceeds 80% threshold, restart pods sequentially using oc rollout restart deployment/mfs-payment-gateway -n mfs-payments. If persistent, increase pool size in payment-config ConfigMap.

2. Tokenization HSM Timeout
Symptom: TokenizationService latency spike, PKCS#11 session timeout errors.
Diagnosis: Verify hsm-gateway.mfs.internal:8443 health endpoint. Check HSM session pool metrics on mfs-vault-pod-01.
Resolution: Restart svc-token-vault sessions. If HSM is unresponsive, escalate to Platform Engineering.

3. Kafka Producer Errors
Symptom: Payment events not reaching webhook dispatcher, consumer lag increasing.
Diagnosis: Check kafka-broker.mfs.internal broker health via kafka-manager. Verify topic mfs.payment.events partition status.
Resolution: If broker is unhealthy, restart affected broker. If topic partitions are offline, reassign partitions.

4. Webhook Delivery Failures
Symptom: DLQ depth increasing, merchants reporting missing notifications.
Diagnosis: Check webhook_dlq table depth. Verify merchant endpoint health via webhook test endpoint (POST /webhooks/{id}/test).
Resolution: If merchant endpoint is down, pause deliveries. Once restored, replay DLQ entries via DeadLetterQueue.replay().

5. Redis Connection Errors
Symptom: Idempotency key lookups failing, duplicate payment risk.
Diagnosis: Verify redis-cluster.mfs.internal cluster status using redis-cli cluster info. Check CLUSTER_STATE and connected_clients.
Resolution: If cluster state is not 'ok', check for failed nodes and perform failover. Restart affected pods to re-establish connections.

Rollback Procedures
- GitLab CI/CD: Trigger rollback-production job in the mfs-payment-gateway pipeline to deploy the previous stable version.
- OpenShift manual: oc rollback deployment/mfs-payment-gateway -n mfs-payments on ocp-prod-east.mfs.internal.
- Database: Rollback migrations via Alembic downgrade if schema changes caused the incident. Coordinate with DBA team.
